text:
Kai: FYI — onboarding Paloma's customer LoRA (paloma-lora-v2.safetensors) into our opus-13b int4 build shows a weird token shift in downstream summaries and invoice amounts. attaching quick eval pack.
Anya: Can you paste the top-line numbers from the eval? rouge/accuracy diffs?
Kai: Quick snapshot from the pack: base opus-13b float -> Rouge-L 46.2; opus-13b-int4 w/ paloma lora -> Rouge-L 40.1; invoice amount extraction F1 drop from 0.92 -> 0.78.
Seb: Oof, that's significant. Could be tokenizer mismatch or a remapping in the quantized path. Any tokenizer changes in the LoRA export?
Kai: LoRA team said they exported using the customer's forked tokenizer (paloma/tokenizer v1.2) but we mapped to our opus tokenizer at merge time. I suspect a subtle vocab offset around currency symbols.
Dani: Reproduced locally. Command I ran: 
```
rwd eval run --model opus-13b-int4 --lora paloma-lora-v2.safetensors --eval-pack packs/paloma_quickpack.json --seed 42 --log-level debug
```
Dani: Debug snippet shows: token ids for '€' = 2874 on our tokenizer, but when applying the LoRA patch weights the kv-cache indexing steps align as if token 2875 was expected — looks like an off-by-one during token->id remap at merge.
Ciara: If it's an off-by-one from remapping, easiest short-term patch is to re-run the merge step with explicit tokenizer alignment: export the LoRA using `--align-tokenizer-path` flag so we canonicalize ids before saving. Example: 
```
python tools/export_lora.py \ 
  --source-lora paloma-lora-v2.safetensors \ 
  --target-tokenizer models/opus-tokenizer \ 
  --align-tokenizer-path paloma/tokenizer
```
Ciara: Longer term we should add a merge-time check that verifies token id histograms and raises if >0.5% mismatch.
Anya: Good plan. For immediate mitigation can we try re-exporting with align flag and re-run the quickpack? Dani can you try?
Dani: On it. Will re-export and push a quick validation run. ETA ~20m.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy for opus-13b-int4 blocked by failing quickpack: paloma_quickpack.json (status: failed) :rotating_light:
Dani: Update — re-exported with explicit alignment, reran eval. New numbers: Rouge-L 45.9, invoice F1 0.91. Major regressions gone.
Kai: Awesome. Looks like align-tokenizer fixed it. Ciara please open a post-merge checklist PR to require alignment for any LoRA that references a non-default tokenizer.
Ciara: Will do. Filing PR + a small unit test that checks token id mapping diffs.
Seb: Also let's add a short note in the onboarding doc for customers: "If you use a custom tokenizer, include the tokenizer artifact in the LoRA upload or request alignment at merge."
Kai: Thanks all — I'll notify Paloma that we have a fix and will re-run their full eval suite overnight. :thumbsup:
